narrative: Material PL2__M4410282 shows smooth, continuously-positive demand (CV=0.393) with a statistically significant upward trend of +141 units per working day. Lead times are moderately stable (CV=0.388, mean=2.76 days). The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock, which is wholly inadequate to meet the 95% service level target. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with safety stock of 55,521 units and a storage-capacity-capped order quantity of 511,366 units is recommended; the storage constraint is binding at 99.9999% utilisation.
warnings: Capacity constraint is binding - order quantity reduced from EOQ 619,034 to 511,366
Optimised policy costs more than previous due to introduction of safety stock from 0 to 55,521 units

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and continuously positive with a detectable upward trend; an EOQ-based (r,Q) model is the textbook-optimal choice for this regime as it minimises total ordering and holding cost while the reorder point absorbs lead-time demand uncertainty.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is binding at 99.9999% utilisation. The capped order quantity (511,366 vs EOQ 619,034) increases replenishment frequency by ~21%, raising annual ordering cost and increasing stockout exposure between deliveries. If demand growth continues, the storage ceiling will become untenable within 12-18 months.
research_insights.escalation_flag: No MOQ-capacity infeasibility. However, near-full storage utilisation warrants a capacity review with the warehouse team to assess whether additional storage or consignment stocking can be arranged.
